title: The Myth of Artificial Intelligence
subtitle: Why Computers Can't Think the Way We Do
publisher: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press
pitch: A computer scientist argues that today's AI cannot do abduction, the everyday leap to the best explanation, and that hype about general AI is a myth that hurts science.

chapters.g: The belief that general AI is coming soon, and how it shapes funding and culture.
Deduction and induction are what machines do well; abduction, guessing the best explanation, is what they lack.
Learning from big data finds patterns, but common sense needs more than patterns.
Why understanding language needs world knowledge machines do not have.
Hype pushes out real science and invites us to undervalue human minds.

ideas: Abductive inference is the missing piece of AI.
Induction from data cannot give common sense.
No one knows how to build general AI.
The myth of inevitable AI harms science.

args.a: Current methods cannot produce general intelligence.
args.c: Since the book, large language models showed abilities many thought needed common sense, though debate continues.
Others think ambitious goals have driven real progress.

questions: Give an example of abduction from your own day.
Did ChatGPT prove Larson wrong, or right?
What would convince you AI has common sense?

quiz.q: What kind of inference does Larson say AI lacks?
quiz.w: The leap to the best explanation.

o: That general AI is inevitable and near
quiz.w: He argues it is not inevitable.
